headings.title: SMTO-EXE-0180 — The document step was stopped before it finished

html:
SMTO-EXE-0180 — The document step was stopped before it finished

GUID: 8f950b90-2182-5516-b84e-942016fe8f6a
Slug: office-operation-cancelled
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: office

What happened

  • The step working on your Word, Excel or PowerPoint file was stopped, ran out of time, or was a repeat of a request already sent. Your original file is never changed, but a new copy from an earlier attempt may exist.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Artifacts under SMTO's reply in this task, and look in any folder you asked SMTO to save to, for a new copy of the document. An earlier attempt of the same step may already have saved its result.
  2. If you find a new copy, open it to check it contains the change you wanted, and use it instead of asking again. Asking again would make a second copy you don't need.
  3. If there is no new copy, ask SMTO to do the step again. If it stopped because it took too long, ask for a smaller change or use a smaller file. A step that runs past its time limit is stopped, so a smaller piece of work can finish in time.

What success looks like

  • You have exactly one new copy of the document with your change in it.

If it still fails

  • If the step keeps stopping before it finishes, select Copy error details and send them, with the file's name and size, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep asking for the same change without checking for new copies first.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Office service returned operation_cancelled because the execution ID was already active or recently finished on this Gateway, or the File layer reported cancellation or timeout.

What this means

  • Office admission found an active/retained execution identity, or File processing reported cancellation or timeout before confirmed publication. Office workers treat document content as untrusted data and never execute macros or formulas. Publication creates a separate output under existing File policy; retain revision and effect facts before any new write.

Why this can happen

  • Office admission found an active/retained execution identity, or File processing reported cancellation or timeout before confirmed publication.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish duplicate admission, user cancellation and deadline using original receipt and output path.

How to fix it

  • Do not resend the same execution ID; the Gateway fences it for five minutes. Check the run's artifacts and any requested output_path for a file from the original attempt, then issue a new, separately approved request only if that output is missing (the operation deadline is 45 seconds).
  • Inspect the original receipt and any output; do not replay a retained execution identity or assume a stopped worker means no publication.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect outputs before a new request. A cancelled or duplicate execution ID is not replayed.

How to verify the fix

  • The original worker and publication state settle before a separately authorized new document operation.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay uncertain writes or execute embedded document content.

Technical notes

  • Office workers treat document content as untrusted data and never execute macros or formulas. Publication creates a separate output under existing File policy; retain revision and effect facts before any new write.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
